items.q: Which serology pattern indicates acute hepatitis B infection?
o: HBsAg negative, anti HBs positive alone
HBsAg positive with IgM anti HBc positive
Anti HBc IgG alone with normal enzymes
HBeAg negative with no other markers
items.exp: Acute hepatitis B shows surface antigen with IgM core antibody (and usually HBeAg). Vaccine immunity shows anti HBs alone without core antibody.
r: Incorrect. That is vaccine induced immunity.
Correct. Surface antigen plus IgM core marks acute infection.
Incorrect. IgG core alone suggests past infection.
Incorrect. HBeAg alone does not stage acuity.
items.kp: Acute B equals surface antigen plus IgM core antibody.

items.q: Anti HBs positive with anti HBc negative most likely means what?
items.exp: Vaccines contain surface antigen only, so immunity shows anti HBs without core antibody. Natural infection exposes core antigen too, leaving both antibodies.
r: Incorrect. Natural infection leaves core antibody as well.
Correct. Surface antibody alone means vaccination.
Incorrect. Carriers retain surface antigen positivity.
Incorrect. Window period shows core IgM as surface markers shift.
items.kp: Surface antibody without core antibody equals vaccine immunity.

items.q: Portal hypertension in cirrhosis produces which clinical triad?
o: Encephalopathy, fetor and flapping tremor alone
items.exp: Raised portal pressure plus splanchnic vasodilation causes ascites, portosystemic varices and congestive splenomegaly. The other sets reflect cholestasis, encephalopathy or hyperoestrogenism respectively.
r: Incorrect. That triad reflects cholestasis.
Correct. Ascites, varices and splenomegaly mark portal hypertension.
Incorrect. Those mark encephalopathy features.
Incorrect. Those are chronic liver stigmata of hormone imbalance.
items.kp: Portal triad: fluid, varices, big spleen.

items.q: Mallory Denk bodies within ballooned hepatocytes with neutrophils most suggest what?
o: Alcohol related hepatitis (also seen in metabolic steatohepatitis)
items.exp: Mallory Denk bodies are keratin aggregates in ballooned hepatocytes with neutrophilic satellitosis, classic for alcohol hepatitis but mirrored in metabolic steatohepatitis and Wilson disease.
r: Incorrect. Viral disease shows lobular spotty necrosis instead.
Correct. This pattern means steatohepatitis, usually alcohol related.
Incorrect. Interface hepatitis has plasma cell rich portal attack.
Incorrect. Iron stains with Prussian blue in haemochromatosis.
items.kp: Mallory bodies plus neutrophils equals steatohepatitis pattern.

items.q: Hepatic encephalopathy in cirrhosis is driven mainly by what bypassing hepatic detoxification?
o: Gut derived ammonia and neurotoxins via portosystemic shunts
items.exp: Ammonia and other gut toxins bypass the failing liver through shunts and impair astrocyte function, causing encephalopathy graded from subtle confusion to coma, precipitated by bleeding, infection and constipation.
r: Incorrect. Bilirubin causes jaundice, not encephalopathy directly.
Correct. Shunted gut ammonia drives encephalopathy.
Incorrect. Albumin falls, not rises, in cirrhosis.
Incorrect. Copper drives Wilson disease neurology differently.
items.kp: Bleed, infection or constipation plus confusion: treat encephalopathy triggers.

items.q: Interface hepatitis with plasma cells and rosettes on biopsy most suggests which hepatitis type?
items.exp: Autoimmune hepatitis attacks the limiting plate (interface hepatitis) with plasma cell rich infiltrates, hepatocyte rosettes and autoantibodies, responding to immunosuppression unlike viral patterns.
r: Incorrect. Hepatitis A is acute lobular without chronic interface pattern.
Correct. Interface plus plasma cells means autoimmune hepatitis.
Incorrect. Alcohol gives steatohepatitis with Mallory bodies.
Incorrect. Ischaemia gives centrilobular necrosis after hypotension.
items.kp: Plasma cells at the interface point autoimmune. Suppress immunity.

items.q: Acute liver failure is defined by coagulopathy plus encephalopathy in which setting?
o: No prior chronic liver disease, illness under weeks
items.exp: Acute liver failure requires INR prolongation with encephalopathy in a patient without pre existing cirrhosis, developing within weeks, with cerebral oedema as the early killer.
r: Incorrect. That describes decompensated chronic disease instead.
Correct. New liver, clotting failure and encephalopathy define it.
Incorrect. Jaundice alone lacks the failure criteria.
Incorrect. Enzyme rise without failure is hepatitis, not failure.
items.kp: No cirrhosis plus clotting failure plus coma risk: refer for transplant now.

items.q: Hepatitis E becomes fulminant most notoriously in which group?
items.exp: Hepatitis E causes fulminant failure with high mortality in pregnancy (especially third trimester in endemic regions), while usually self limiting otherwise except in immunosuppression where it chronicises.
r: Correct. Pregnancy makes hepatitis E fulminant.
Incorrect. Vaccination is not the risk setting described.
Incorrect. Superinfection concepts belong to delta with B instead.
Incorrect. Maternal immunity protects rather than endangers newborns here.
items.kp: Pregnant plus hepatitis E equals fulminant danger.

items.q: Hepatitis D (delta) virus can only infect in presence of which virus and why?
o: Hepatitis B, needing surface antigen coat
items.exp: Delta is a defective virus borrowing hepatitis B surface antigen as its envelope, so it co infects or superinfects B carriers, worsening severity. Preventing B prevents D.
r: Incorrect. C plays no coating role for delta.
Correct. Delta needs hepatitis B surface antigen.
Incorrect. A shares route but not structure with delta.
Incorrect. HIV tropism is unrelated to delta assembly.
items.kp: No B, no D: vaccinate against B to block both.

items.q: Centrilobular (zone 3) necrosis after a hypotensive shock episode indicates what?
items.exp: Zone 3 around central veins is furthest from oxygen supply, so shock and cardiac failure cause centrilobular necrosis with massive transaminase spikes that recover quickly if perfusion returns (ischaemic hepatitis).
r: Incorrect. Autoimmunity attacks portal interfaces chronically.
Correct. Shock liver necroses zone 3.
Incorrect. Viral hepatitis gives lobular spotty patterns.
Incorrect. Obstruction dilates ducts with cholestatic enzymes.
items.kp: Shock plus huge enzymes plus zone 3 necrosis equals ischaemic hepatitis.
